stories.title: Ghana marks World Mental Health Day with focus on lived experience
stories.summary: People with lived experience of mental health conditions took centre stage at a grand durbar in Tamale to mark World Mental Health Day. Stakeholders called for stronger action to reduce stigma and expand livelihood opportunities, emphasising the importance of involving those affected in decisions that impact their lives.

Minnesota addresses collective trauma and mental health
stories.summary: Minnesota has faced a series of high-profile events in recent years, including the murder of George Floyd and the assassination of a House Speaker. The state branch of the National Alliance on Mental Illness is now working to address the resulting toll on the collective mental health of residents.

stories.title: Sangamon County Mental Health Board to hold community forum
stories.summary: The Sangamon County Mental Health Board will host a community forum on November 30 to present its one-year plan. Executive director Dr. Tatyana Gardner said the event aims to identify service gaps and gather feedback from residents who have navigated the local mental health care system.

stories.title: Texas Veterans Commission offers mental health resources
stories.summary: The Texas Veterans Commission provides programs to help veterans and their families manage mental health challenges after service. Operations managers and supervisors are currently highlighting how these resources function and how veterans across the state can access the department's support services.

stories.title: Study finds one in four students use AI for mental health support
stories.summary: A peer-reviewed study of 2,020 students at a UK university found that one in four used AI for mental health support in the past six months. Many students turned to the tools when distressed, with usage highest among those reporting very low well-being.

stories.title: UND supports pilot mental health program for aviation students
stories.summary: The University of North Dakota is supporting the UpLift peer support program to help aviation students navigate mental health concerns. The initiative aims to remove barriers to seeking help, as students often fear that diagnoses or treatments could jeopardise their flight training and future careers.

stories.title: Parents remain skeptical of AI mental health chatbots for children
stories.summary: A study published in JAMA Pediatrics found that 76 percent of parents are uncomfortable with the use of AI-powered treatment for children. Despite a national therapist shortage and rising youth mental health concerns, parents expressed significant worry regarding the accuracy of AI tools.

Adya Retreats combines neuroscience with wellness practices
stories.summary: Adya Retreats is a nomadic wellness programme that uses EEG brain scans alongside breathwork, yoga, and meditation. The retreats, curated by Shivangi Sharma, aim to explore the relationship between brain activity and mind-body practices during multi-day sessions held in various locations across India.

stories.title: Study finds lawyer burnout persists despite wellness initiatives
stories.summary: A study of 39,000 US lawyers published in the Journal of Affective Disorders suggests that a decade of wellness programs and mindfulness sessions has produced little improvement in mental health. In some cases, the report notes that wellness metrics for legal professionals have actually worsened.

stories.title: UCLA marks 20 years of mindfulness research
stories.summary: UCLA behavioral geneticist Sue Smalley established a meditation room on campus in 2002 after personal health challenges inspired her to study the science of mindfulness. The university has since spent two decades researching the practice, long before it became a common household term.

stories.title: Study finds reduced loneliness after two-week ChatGPT break
stories.summary: A randomized trial of 625 active ChatGPT users found that those who stopped using AI assistants for two weeks reported feeling less lonely. Participants also engaged in more in-person social interactions during the pause, with improvements in loneliness persisting for two weeks after the trial ended.

stories.title: Meditation gains mainstream attention in wellness discourse
stories.summary: Meditation has moved from niche practice to mainstream interest, with corporations appointing Chief Mindfulness Officers and politicians calling for a mindful nation. Research into the practice continues to examine its impact on physical and emotional well-being as it becomes an increasingly common feature of modern life.

stories.title: Sound healing gains popularity as a mainstream wellness practice
stories.summary: Sound healing has transitioned from a niche holistic practice to a mainstream therapy in recent years. Practitioners suggest that the rise in popularity is driven by people seeking alternative ways to regulate their nervous systems and find calm in a chaotic world.

stories.title: Lawsuit filed over human cost of mining in Congo
stories.summary: Residents in Kolwezi are suing a mining company and the government, alleging that pollution from copper and cobalt operations has caused severe health issues. The lawsuit represents a rare attempt to hold companies accountable for the human cost associated with the electric vehicle supply chain.

Sydney researchers identify circadian depression subtype
stories.summary: University of Sydney researchers identified a new subtype of depression linked to the body's internal 24-hour clock. The condition, dubbed circadian depression, appeared in nearly 25 percent of participants with severe or persistent depression. The researchers hope the classification will lead to more targeted medical and behavioral treatments.

stories.title: Researchers Identify Circadian Depression Subtype Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients - SSBCrack News
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Sydney have identified a potential subtype of depression closely linked to the body’s internal biological clock. The condition, described as “circadian depression,” may help explain why some people respond less well,or experience more side effects,from commonly prescribed antidepressants. stories.summary: Despite leaving Strictly Come Dancing after 21 years, Tess Daly hasn’t left movement behind. Now 57, the presenter has spoken about a fitness routine built around dancing, rebounding and strength training to with walks and yoga helping her find time to switch off. stories.summary: Most people first start exercising when they have knee pain, back stiffness, or trouble ascending a flight of stairs. stories.title: Frequent short walks may better regulate blood sugar
stories.summary: Taking frequent, short walks throughout the day improved blood sugar regulation more than completing the same amount of exercise in one continuous session, according to a study of 30 participants in the journal Obesity. The findings suggest that those who sit all day might reconsider their movement routines.

Study links healthier school meals to academic performance
stories.summary: A study published in Public Health Nutrition evaluated the Eat Real program, which certifies schools that serve meals prepared from scratch rather than ultra-processed ingredients. Researchers found an association between the program and improved academic outcomes in K-12 students. The organization advocates for real food in schools.

stories.title: Quebecers improving diet choices despite food quality
stories.summary: A study from Université Laval found that Quebecers are making better dietary choices despite little improvement in the nutritional quality of available prepackaged foods. Lead researcher Véronique Provencher noted that the study allowed for both quantifying and qualifying the population's diet. The food supply remains largely unchanged.

stories.title: Gut Doctor Explains Which Foods Are Actually Linked To Chronic Inflammation
stories.summary: From plant-based burgers to your morning coffee sweetener, what you eat can definitely affect your gut. But certain foods actually contribute to chronic inflammation. Which ones deserve your attention, and which viral food warnings can you safely ignore? In a video titled A Gut Doctor’s 5 Foods That Drive Chronic

Fermented foods and aging
stories.summary: A new review examines whether fermented foods like yogurt and kimchi influence inflammation and cellular health. Researchers are exploring if these dietary staples offer benefits that extend beyond digestion to the aging process. The review synthesizes existing studies on the potential role of fermented foods in healthy aging.

stories.title: Peeling Your Produce? You Could Be Throwing Away Extra Fiber - Food & Wine
Zinc deficiency and the gut microbiome
stories.summary: A Cornell University study suggests that chronic zinc deficiency rewires the intestinal tract, with the small intestine and colon responding differently. Published in Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology, the research maps how zinc availability shapes the relationship between the gut lining and its resident microbes.

stories.title: Common Medications May Affect Your Gut Years After You Stop Taking Them, Scientists Say - Men's Journal
Education and dementia risk
stories.summary: An extra year of required schooling is linked to fewer dementia cases later in life, particularly for those with high genetic risk. While some medications can slow dementia progression, no current treatment can reverse it. Researchers suggest that increased schooling may serve as a potential risk-reduction intervention.

stories.title: Dolphin social stability and longevity
stories.summary: Wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins with predictable group sizes and higher sociability tend to live longer, according to a study in PLOS Biology. Researchers found that an individual dolphin's average group size fluctuates across its lifespan. Stability in social grouping appears to correlate directly with longevity.

stories.title: Can Reading Books Increase Your Lifespan? What the Research Says About Longevity Benefits - Verywell Mind
Exercise versus diet for longevity
stories.summary: A review in Mayo Clinic Proceedings suggests that regular movement and cardiorespiratory fitness are more strongly associated with longevity than diet quality alone. Researchers assessed dozens of studies on mortality risk. While poor diet is linked to higher risk, the association is smaller than that of exercise.

stories.title: Generational shifts in longevity
stories.summary: Consumers increasingly view exercise, sleep, and diet as the primary drivers of healthspan, according to insights presented at the Nutra Healthspan Summit. Belief in the impact of genetics varies significantly by age, with 39 percent of those aged 65 and over citing it as a major factor.

stories.title: Exercise holds a stronger link to longevity than diet
stories.summary: A narrative review in Mayo Clinic Proceedings suggests that physical activity has a stronger relationship to longevity than diet. Exercise physiologist Glenn Gaesser notes that in every instance studied, cardiorespiratory fitness proved more significant. The findings challenge the assumption that diet and exercise are equally weighted for lifespan.

stories.title: Yoga and biological aging
stories.summary: A review published in Cureus found that while yoga improves physical functioning, balance, and strength in older adults, evidence is insufficient to conclude that it slows biological aging. Researchers examined studies on cardiovascular health, brain function, and physical performance to assess the practice's impact on aging markers.

stories.title: AI and the human biological clock
stories.summary: As AI models approach human expert intelligence, the digital world accelerates, yet human biology remains unchanged. Despite the cultural push to leverage technology for longevity, the body continues to follow its own clock. Exhaustion cannot be cleared with one click, regardless of the pace of digital innovation.

stories.title: Yale analysis of anti-aging interventions
stories.summary: A Yale analysis published in Nature Medicine evaluated 51 studies on anti-aging diets, drugs, and supplements. By testing over 3,000 samples against 16 epigenetic clocks, researchers sought to determine which interventions actually influence biological aging. The study aims to identify what truly moves the needle in longevity research.

stories.title: Ayurvedic therapies and wellness tourism
stories.summary: Traditional Ayurvedic therapies are fueling a boom in India's wellness tourism industry. While the ancient system emphasizes restoring natural balance through herbs and diet, scientific evidence regarding its effectiveness remains insufficient. The industry continues to use these practices as a primary selling point for international and domestic visitors.

The agreement was signed on November 20, 2026, in Chennai, marking a step towards translating

stories.title: SRMIST licenses poly-herbal diabetes technology
stories.summary: SRM Institute of Science and Technology has licensed a patented poly-herbal formulation to Dr. SHREEVARMA’s Wellness Private Limited. The non-exclusive agreement aims to translate academic research into commercial products for diabetes support. The technology was developed by the university's Interdisciplinary Institute of Indian System of Medicine.

stories.title: Researchers propose multi-omics framework for Ayurvedic study
stories.summary: Researchers at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham have proposed a multi-omics framework to evaluate Ayurvedic therapies for diminished ovarian reserve. The authors suggest this approach may address why conventional single-target strategies often fail to yield reliable clinical benefits. The study remains an opinion paper on potential methodology.

stories.title: Sterling resorts promote wellness tourism for Ayurveda Day
stories.summary: Sterling resorts are marketing Ayurvedic therapies and spa experiences as part of their guest offerings across India. The company frames these services as a way for travellers to slow down and reconnect with their bodies. Wellness is now a standard amenity in the hospitality sector.

stories.title: Ayurveda retreats see rise in visitor numbers
stories.summary: India is seeing an increase in visitors to wellness retreats offering traditional Ayurvedic treatments. Practitioners describe the practices as a way to restore the body's natural balance through herbal regimes and yoga. The clinical effectiveness of these centuries-old methods remains a subject of ongoing scientific study.

stories.title: Ayurveda retreats grow amid global wellness interest
stories.summary: India's government is promoting the ancient Ayurveda system as a form of traditional healthcare. While retreats promise holistic health through herbal treatments and yoga, there is limited scientific evidence supporting their effectiveness. The wellness sector continues to expand despite the lack of clinical validation.

research.summary: Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe.
